title: Derived generation of supported norm-coefficient finite local models by finite-field scalar extensions
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with its extended $\ell$-adic norm topology. Put $B(P)=C(P,\Omega)$, using all continuous maps on every profinite set $P$, and $A_F(P)=C(P,F)$ for each finite intermediate field $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq F\subseteq\Omega$, with its restricted norm topology [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Put $R_V=p_V^*R$ for these condensed rings on each scheme $V$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Work with internal module objects on small pro-étale sites and their ordinary uncompleted derived categories in the fixed indexing universe [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, def-weil-size-convention].
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. A support chain over $X$ is a finite chain $W=X_s\to\cdots\to X_0=X$ whose arrows are quasi-compact open immersions or closed immersions with quasi-compact open complement [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Write $J_B$ for the composite of $a_!$ on open arrows and $a_*$ on closed arrows, with the identity for the empty chain [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek, def-sfb-module-lower-star]. A finite scalar local model is a module pro-étale locally isomorphic to $B_V\otimes_{\underline\Omega}\underline P$ for a finitely presented scalar $\Omega$-module $P$; the scalar modules and finite ranks may vary among cover members [sk-def-sfb-constructible].

Let $\mathscr G_X$ be the intersection of all full replete classes of objects of $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{B_X})$ satisfying the following explicit conditions. They contain zero and every
$$J_B(B_W\otimes_{A_{E,W}}N)[0],$$
where the support chain, finite intermediate field $E$ and pro-étale locally finite free $A_{E,W}$-module $N$ vary independently [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module, sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. They are closed under all integer shifts, distinguished-triangle extensions and retracts [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]; a retract is a diagram $K\xrightarrow{i}L\xrightarrow{p}K$ with $pi=1_K$. They are closed under all small products in the ordinary derived category [def-weil-category-product]. Finally, for every strict small filtered diagram of $B_X$-module complexes $K_i^\bullet$ with one common termwise lower bound and $QK_i^\bullet$ in the class for every $i$, the class contains $Q(\varinjlim_iK_i^\bullet)$, with termwise sheaf colimit and localization $Q$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. This paragraph defines the class, and asserts no closure property of any other subcategory.

For every support chain over $X$ and every finite scalar local model $L$ on its source one has
$$J_B L[0]\in\mathscr G_X.$$
There is no closed pair, torsion-rigidity or cohomology-comparison assumption. The generators have finite-field models; the conclusion does not supply any finite-field model or finite field for the transition maps of $L$. No Noetherianity, characteristic, dimension, completeness of $\Omega$, or finite-subextension-valued replacement of $B$ is imposed. Empty schemes, rank zero and the empty chain are included.

proof.text: Fix a support chain with source $W$. Every vertex is qcqs: a quasi-compact open has a finite affine cover, and a closed subscheme has the closed preimages of a finite affine cover; its affine overlaps are closed in quasi-compact overlaps of the ambient scheme. Closed-subset quasi-compactness and the affine-overlap criterion give the assertion inductively. If $W$ is empty, $J_BL=0$ and the result follows. Otherwise the finitely presented scalar $\Omega$-modules in a trivializing cover have finite bases: a basis is contained in the span of the finitely many supplied generators and hence is finite. Finite-free scalar extension identifies the local models with finite powers of $B$. Take a finite affine refinement $b_a:U_a\to W$ of this cover, and choose frames $L|_{U_a}\simeq B_{U_a}^{r_a}$. Set $U=\coprod_aU_a$ and $b:U\to W$. The finite-family site geometry makes $b$ a qcqs covering object and identifies $h_U=\coprod_a h_{U_a}$.

proof.text: Write $U_n=U\times_W\cdots\times_WU$ ($n+1$ factors), $b_n:U_n\to W$ and $L_n=b_n^*L$. The finite-family site geometry and qcqs permanence show that every $U_n$ and $b_n$ is qcqs; no affineness or weak contractibility of these fibre products is claimed. Put $r=\max_a r_a$. The first projection $U_n\to U$ partitions $U_n$ into finitely many clopen subschemes carrying the pulled-back frames. On its $a$-th piece, embed $B^{r_a}$ in the first $r_a$ coordinates of $B^r$ and project back onto those coordinates. These maps glue over the disjoint pieces and their composite is the identity of $L_n$. Thus $L_n$ is a retract of $B_{U_n}^r$. The regular-chart lemma puts $Rb_{n*}B_{U_n}[0]$ in $\mathscr G_W$. The additive derived direct image sends this retraction to a retraction and preserves finite biproducts; these identities follow termwise on finite sums of injective resolutions. Hence $Rb_{n*}L_n[0]\in\mathscr G_W$, using finite products and retract closure. The frames and retraction maps may use arbitrary continuous $\Omega$-valued coefficients.

proof.text: Apply the normalized Čech pushforward-model theorem with $f=\mathrm{id}$ on $W_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$, the epimorphic cover $h_U\to1$, and $N=L$. The localization of the site at $U_n$ is its own pro-étale site; the internal/section-module equivalence identifies all actual module operations. The theorem supplies one coherent first-quadrant complex $D^{n,q}$, column isomorphisms $QD^{n,\bullet}\simeq Rb_{n*}L_n[0]$, and an augmentation isomorphism $L[0]\simeq Q\operatorname{Tot}D$. This uses the theorem's stated coherent model, rather than assigning a total to a diagram only in the triangulated homotopy category. Termwise products compute derived products on the pro-étale module category. Apply the first-quadrant product-hull lemma with $\mathcal H=\mathscr G_W$ and the column membership from the preceding step. It gives $L[0]\in\mathscr G_W$. All diagrams are in the fixed universe and every resolution degree is nonnegative.

proof.text: We now pass from $W$ back to $X$ along the fixed support chain. Each open $j_!$ and closed $i_*$ is exact on module sheaves, hence induces a triangulated termwise functor. The exact internal/section-module equivalences identify these with the functors defining $J_B$. For quasi-compact opens the extension-zero limit theorem gives preservation of all small products, both on sheaves and on derived categories. A closed direct image is right adjoint to its module inverse image, so preserves sheaf products; since products are computed termwise in both pro-étale derived categories and $i_*$ is exact, it preserves their derived products as well. Therefore $J_B$ preserves shifts, distinguished triangles, products and retractions.

proof.text: For a strict small filtered diagram of complexes with one common termwise lower bound, every open $j_!$ commutes with its termwise colimit because it is left adjoint to $j^*$. Every closed $i_*$ commutes with filtered sheaf colimits by the qcqs ringed open–closed theorem. Thus $J_B$ commutes with the required termwise colimits and preserves their common lower bound. Let $\mathcal H=\{K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{B_W}):J_BK\in\mathscr G_X\}$. Step 4 and this colimit calculation give every closure axiom defining $\mathscr G_W$ for $\mathcal H$. It contains every generator of $\mathscr G_W$: applying $J_B$ just concatenates its support chain with the fixed chain over $X$, leaving its finite field $E$ and lisse $A_E$-model unchanged. It also contains zero. By the defining intersection, $\mathscr G_W\subseteq\mathcal H$. The membership $L[0]\in\mathscr G_W$ proved in step 3 therefore yields $J_BL[0]\in\mathscr G_X$. This uses no finite field for the transition maps of $L$. Rank zero and the empty chain require no change.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NE-f79fa7776 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, both new nodes in full, every cited statement and the blueprint refinement proof (main-20261024). The statement is unchanged; the proof is agent-written and the WANTED line is honest. Steps: (1) Chain vertices are qcqs by closed-in-qc and the affine-cover criterion. Empty W is handled first, as the finite affine refinement node needs a nonempty scheme. Finitely presented Omega-modules are finite free, and B tensor Omega^r is B^r. (2) Each L_n is a coordinate retract of B^r on the clopen pieces given by the first projection; the regular-chart node applies with X=W and b=b_n qcqs; G_W is closed under finite products and retracts. (3) The Cech pushforward model with f=id and h_U->1 gives the columns and the augmentation; its sign delta+(-1)^n d matches the new totalisation node; det-pe-products-derived supplies the termwise-product hypothesis. (4) j_! preserves derived products by det-sf-open-closed-extension-zero-limits (2). i_* is exact and right adjoint, so it preserves products termwise. (5) j_! is a left adjoint and i_* commutes with filtered colimits on qcqs schemes. The preimage class contains the generators because support chains concatenate. New node lem-sfb-first-quadrant-product-hull-total: I checked it is true. The finite-column truncations are quotient complexes, each kernel is a shifted column, the tower is split and degreewise stable, and the sequence 0->T->prod T_m->prod T_m->0 is exact. My search found no duplicate; the same argument appears only inside the proof of supported-hull-proetale-descent, not in its statement. New node lem-sfb-norm-regular-chart-finite-field-hull: self-contained, statement-only, and not a restatement of the item. Small cases tested: b=id, U empty, finite unions of identity charts. Its hard case, a separably closed point with a profinite chart, i.e. C(S,Omega), coincides with the already accepted open node proetale-supported-model-coinduction (Lambda=Omega), because the two hulls agree on such a point. It is not D2: the item keeps the Cech reconstruction and the totalisation, which remove the transition-function problem. I accept the 9 declared tool_uses as generic tools. No changes.
